Job Title: Head of Group Benefits Enrollment and Billing Technology
Job Description: Head of Group Benefits Enrollment and Billing Technology Position Overview As the Head of Group Benefits Enrollment and Billing Technology, you will serve as the strategic and technical leader for the capabilities that onboard members, manage eligibility and enrollment, and enable accurate, timely billing across the Group Benefits value stream. You will guide multiple products and squads while partnering closely with business product managers and owners to shape and execute a modern technology vision. Your leadership will simplify complex processes, modernize core platforms, strengthen data quality and controls, and drive secure, resilient delivery aligned to business value—fueling Guardian’s transformation and “Journey to 2030.” You will also be a force multiplier for our engineering community, cultivating the next generation of technology leaders across enrollment and billing. Through hands-on mentorship, coaching, and role-model leadership, you will inspire teams to deepen their domain expertise, strengthen engineering discipline, and embrace continuous improvement. You will champion automation, observability, quality engineering, and modern delivery practices that improve accuracy, throughput, and customer and partner experiences. Your leadership will transform strategy into measurable outcomes across the enrollment-to-billing lifecycle. You will translate ambitious business goals into clear, outcome-driven roadmaps; orchestrate complex initiatives spanning plan setup, eligibility, enrollment, member data, billing, payments, and integrations; and shape investment decisions with a strong focus on operational efficiency, financial accuracy, and risk reduction. You will partner across Value Stream, Platform, Data, AI, Finance, Operations, and Enterprise teams to drive alignment, scale, and sustained momentum. You Will (Responsibilities) Set and champion the domain-level technology strategy and architectural vision for Group Benefits enrollment and billing, ensuring products and platforms evolve cohesively toward a modern, scalable future. Translate business strategies into multi-year modernization plans that simplify the enrollment-to-billing journey, retire legacy complexity, and improve speed, accuracy, and service outcomes. Own end-to-end technology outcomes across plan setup, eligibility, enrollment, member and coverage data, billing, adjustments, payments, reconciliation, and related partner integrations. Oversee technical design and data governance, ensuring performance, resilience, security, auditability, and financial controls remain uncompromising across squads and platforms. Build and scale reusable engineering patterns, APIs, event-driven integrations, data quality controls, and automation that reduce manual work and improve straight-through processing. Serve as the trusted escalation point for complex technical decisions, production incidents, enrollment defects, billing discrepancies, and architectural risks—providing clarity, direction, and decisive leadership. Develop, mentor, and elevate engineers, tech leads, quality engineering professionals, and future leaders—strengthening both technical depth and enrollment and billing domain expertise. Partner with Enrollment, Billing, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, Customer Service, Data & AI, and enterprise platform stakeholders to drive cross-domain alignment and unified outcomes. Collaborate with business product managers and owners to define clear quarterly plans, outcomes, dependencies, controls, and commitments that map directly to value stream OKRs. Influence funding prioritization and investment decisions using measurable business outcomes such as improved enrollment quality, billing accuracy, operational efficiency, platform reliability, and customer satisfaction. Drive continuous improvement in automation, SDLC maturity, cloud adoption, observability, engineering tooling, release quality, and production support. Enable teams to apply AI and intelligent automation to reduce enrollment exceptions, improve billing issue detection, accelerate resolution, and enhance employee productivity. Establish and uphold world-class engineering standards—CI/CD, testing, security, supportability, data quality, controls, and metrics—ensuring consistent excellence across all products. You Have (Required Skills) 10+ years of technology or engineering experience, including demonstrated success leading strategy, architecture, and delivery for complex enterprise platforms. A proven track record modernizing legacy systems and delivering platform engineering, process automation, and operational improvements at enterprise scale. Strong knowledge of group benefits, employee benefits, insurance, or adjacent financial-services domains; direct experience with eligibility, enrollment, billing, payments, or reconciliation is strongly preferred. Deep technical expertise across distributed systems, cloud architectures, APIs, integration patterns, data platforms, event-driven design, security, and modern engineering practices. Demonstrated ability to improve data quality, financial accuracy, operational controls, resilience, and customer outcomes across complex business processes. The ability to shape long-term technology strategy, influence architectural direction, manage investment tradeoffs, and lead through ambiguity and organizational change. A history of building high-performing, inclusive engineering cultures that attract, grow, and retain exceptional technical talent. Strong executive-level communication, with the ability to align senior leaders, business and technology partners, and cross-functional teams around measurable outcomes. Location: Hybrid Work arrangement with three days a week at a Guardian office in Holmdel, NJ, Bethlehem, PA or New York, NY. Salary Range: $155,340.00 - $255,210.00 The salary range reflected above is a good faith estimate of base pay for the primary location of the position. Are you energized by collaborating across functions to influence business decisions and drive measurable results? Guardian is seeking a Network Strategy & Delivery Consultant to join the Dental Network Strategy & Strategic Partnerships team within Group Benefits Product & Digital. In this role, you will help shape the future of Guardian's dental provider network by leveraging data-driven insights to develop and execute growth, retention, and profitability strategies. You will have the opportunity to work directly with senior leaders, lead strategic initiatives from concept through implementation, and influence decisions that impact one of Guardian's most important strategic assets. You Are A strategic thinker who enjoys transforming complex data into actionable business recommendations. A highly analytical problem solver who can identify opportunities, evaluate alternatives, and influence decision-making through facts and insights. A self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is comfortable navigating ambiguity and changing priorities. A collaborative partner who works effectively across business functions and builds strong relationships with stakeholders at all levels. An effective communicator who can create compelling executive presentations and present recommendations to senior leadership. Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work with large and complex datasets. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Experience developing business cases, strategic recommendations, and executive-level presentations. Experience managing multiple initiatives and driving projects to successful completion. Demonstrated success leading cross-functional initiatives that drive business growth, profitability, or operational improvement. Experience supporting executive decision-making through data analysis and strategic insights. You Will Develop and execute strategies that support the growth, retention, and profitability of Guardian's dental provider network using data analytics, market research, and business insights. Partner with stakeholders across Network Management, Product, Claims, Service, Finance, Actuarial, and other business functions to evaluate opportunities, build consensus, and implement strategic initiatives. Lead strategic projects from analysis through implementation, utilizing project management and change management principles to drive results. Develop and enhance executive reporting and performance dashboards, delivering insights that support business decision-making and network performance management. Create strategic presentations and recommendations for senior leadership, translating complex analyses into clear and actionable business outcomes. Job Title: Head of Group Benefits Business Risk & Resiliency
Job Description: As the Head of Group Benefits Business Risk & Resiliency, you will execute the Risk & Resiliency frameworks for Group Benefits (GB), Guardian’s B2B line of business. You will manage the operational risk profile for GB, aggregating risk across domains (Technology, Cyber, Data, Model, Compliance, Third Party, etc) and ensuring alignment to Guardian’s risk appetite and tolerance. You will enable informed business decision‑making by providing oversight, independent challenge, and proactive risk insights, supported by risk domain experts within Enterprise Risk Management (ERM). You will Act as a trusted advisor to GB Leadership to drive the Risk & Resiliency program according to Guardian standards, in part by facilitating Risk Working Groups on a regular cadence for transparency and accountability. Escalate topics to the appropriate risk committees as warranted. Assess key risks at the Line of Business and process level and ensure visibility into key risk action items through coordination and engagement with business process owners and risk and control partners. Execute the Business Resiliency framework through development of business continuity plans and resiliency solutions for critical dependencies, regular testing, and oversight of plans, and managing business coordination of Disaster Recovery and Crisis Management efforts. Own and drive maintenance of the Risk Register (ServiceNow) for GB, including establishing reporting standards, promoting self‑identification of risks, and ensuring data quality and completeness. Oversee consolidation and synthesis of risk data across all domains to maintain an aggregated residual risk profile, assess alignment to risk appetite, identify material risk themes and trends, and inform LOB leadership and risk governance discussions. Coordinate and integrate risk activities, including issues, events, Key Risk Indicators(KRIs), and stress scenario analysis, ensuring appropriate linkage, escalation, and consistency across domains. Drive a risk‑aware culture, enabling first‑line ownership of risk and partnering with Business Risk Coordinators to promote consistent standards, effective issue identification, and timely escalation. You are A confident, visible leader and trusted advisor comfortable operating in a highly transparent environment, engaging senior leaders, risk committees, and cross‑functional stakeholders to support informed business decision‑making. A change leader with strong business acumen who provides clear risk insights, credible challenges, and pragmatic trade‑off perspectives to advance business priorities. An exceptional communicator and collaborative relationship builder with a proven ability to partner across lines of business, risk domains, and enterprise functions to drive outcomes through others. You have Required 5+ years of experience in Group Benefits insurance Strong analytical, decision making and problem-solving skills. Preferred 5 yrs in operational risk management or a related risk discipline Flexibility and resourcefulness in managing multiple priorities. The ability to accelerate impact and the desire to lead change. Strong influencing skills with transformational initiatives Reporting Relationship This position is an individual contributor reporting to the Head of Business Risk & Resiliency, who reports to our Chief Risk Officer within Enterprise Risk Management. Job Description: As an individual contributor and Senior Specialist on the Controls Assurance team (within the corporate Internal Audit function), you will support the Head of Business, Controls Assurance with the assessment and execution of internal controls over financial reporting. The company complies with the NAIC Model Audit Rule (MAR), similar to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). This entails internal controls testing and documentation, assessing the impact of control deficiencies, building relationships, and providing guidance to process and controls owners across business and functional areas, and facilitating the needed certifications/signoffs from management. In addition, you will be performing direct assistance controls testing in support of the Company’s external audit. This is a highly visible role collaborating with various levels of management and staff personnel throughout the enterprise as well as with the external audit firm. You are A collaborative, detail-oriented audit professional with experience supporting internal control programs, including Model Audit Rule (MAR), Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), or similar regulatory control frameworks. Knowledgeable about business processes, financial reporting risks, and related key controls, with strong organizational skills and the ability to meet program milestones and deadlines. Skilled at building trusted relationships with business partners, control owners, and audit stakeholders across a complex organization. Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment and demonstrating effective project management, communication, and problem-solving skills. You have Required Qualifications: Minimum 3+ years of relevant experience in internal or external audit, accounting, and/or finance, Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), Model Audit Rule. A bachelor’s degree or equivalent in relevant fields of study - Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or Management, Management Information Systems, or another related field. Strong written and oral communication skills. Sound analytical skills, with the ability to effectively analyze a process and assess risks and controls. Strong project management skills to meet established deadlines. Ability to solve problems and identify root causes of process breakdowns. Ability to collaborate with others, both inside and outside of the department, while working toward common goals and fostering understanding and agreement. Preferred Qualifications: A master’s degree or equivalent. Experience with TeamMate+. Professional accreditations (CIA, CPA, CFE, CISA, etc.), licenses, or designations (MBA). You will Support annual risk assessment, scoping, and planning activities Conduct the annual risk assessment and support completion of MAR scoping and planning activities. Review risk assessment and scoping results with stakeholders and help finalize the MAR program scope. Identify opportunities to use data analytics, automation, and artificial intelligence to enhance scoping and planning activities. Execute and support the annual MAR program Execute key components of the MAR lifecycle in accordance with established methodologies, regulatory expectations, and program timelines. Identify opportunities to apply data analytics, automation, and artificial intelligence capabilities to improve program execution. Manage assigned responsibilities effectively and efficiently while meeting established program deadlines. Support control owners and business testers by monitoring testing progress, answering questions, and helping resolve execution challenges. Communicate progress, challenges, and results clearly to the Controls Assurance team management and business stakeholders. Work with process owners to evaluate control deficiencies, develop remediation recommendations, and support preparation of deficiency documentation. Perform follow-up activities for open deficiencies and monitor progress toward timely resolution. Perform quality assurance reviews to help confirm testing is complete, accurate, and aligned with program methodology. Gather sub-certification deliverables and help identify and address obstacles to MAR attestation. Support external audit deliverables and special projects Respond to external auditor requests in a timely, complete, and well-documented manner. Perform assigned control testing in support of the Company’s external audit. Participate in special projects and ad hoc control initiatives that support departmental and company objectives. Reporting Relationship As our Senior Specialist, Controls Assurance, you will report to our Head of Business, Controls Assurance, who reports to our Head of Internal Audit, Corporate Functions & Controls Assurance. Job Description: Job Summary The Technology Delivery Manager, Technology Operations is accountable for coordinating and driving the successful delivery of strategic and operational technology initiatives across the Technology Operations organization. The role provides a centralized view of priorities, commitments, dependencies, risks, and outcomes while enabling teams to execute with clarity, discipline, and speed. Partnering closely with Technology Operations leadership and delivery teams, this role strengthens execution rigor, delivery transparency, and predictable outcomes across infrastructure operations, resilience, lifecycle management, observability, data management, middleware, cloud operations, and recovery initiatives. Essential Responsibilities Technology Portfolio & Delivery Management Own the integrated delivery portfolio for Technology Operations across all functional domains. Lead initiative intake, prioritization, sequencing, capacity alignment, and dependency management in partnership with Technology Operations leadership. Establish practical and consistent delivery practices, tools, decision forums, and governance across the portfolio. Delivery Planning & Execution Drive initiatives from definition through implementation and transition to operations, ensuring clear outcomes, scope, ownership, milestones, and acceptance criteria. Develop and maintain integrated delivery plans covering milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and mitigation actions. Monitor delivery performance and proactively resolve execution risks, resource constraints, cross-team dependencies, and impediments. Facilitate cross-functional execution while maintaining clear accountability for commitments and outcomes. Stakeholder Management & Communication Serve as the primary point of coordination for Technology Operations delivery status, risks, dependencies, decisions, and escalations. Prepare and deliver concise executive communications, portfolio dashboards, decision materials, and outcome-based status reporting. Facilitate leadership reviews, delivery forums, dependency discussions, and escalation paths as needed. Governance, Reporting & Compliance Implement standardized reporting for delivery health, milestones, risks, dependencies, financials, and realized outcomes across the portfolio. Ensure delivery activities align with enterprise governance, audit, compliance, resilience testing, and regulatory readiness requirements. Use delivery insights, retrospectives, and lessons learned to improve ways of working and execution performance. Execution Enablement Coordinate Technology Operations teams, enterprise partners, vendors, and consultants to align responsibilities, dependencies, and delivery commitments. Enable major transformation, modernization, and resilience initiatives through effective sequencing, resource alignment, and execution governance. Remove delivery friction, accelerate decision-making, and improve predictability across Technology Operations initiatives. Minimum of 8 years of experience leading technology delivery, complex initiatives, or cross-functional execution within enterprise technology environments. Demonstrated experience driving multiple concurrent initiatives across infrastructure, operations, resilience, cloud, platform, or other technology organizations. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level reporting, decision framing, and stakeholder alignment. Proven ability to manage outcomes, risks, dependencies, resources, and cross-team delivery commitments. Since our founding in 1860, our long-term view has helped our customers prepare for whatever life brings whether starting a family, planning for the future, or taking care of employees. Today we’re a Fortune 250 company and a leading provider of life, disability and other benefits for individuals, at the workplace and through government sponsored programs. Are you an experienced IT Asset Management professional who is passionate about establishing trusted asset data, strong lifecycle controls, and effective governance across enterprise hardware and software? Do you excel at balancing operational discipline, license compliance, cost optimization, audit readiness, and partnership across technology and business teams? If so, Guardian Life is looking for an IT Asset Manager to help advance our enterprise IT Asset Management capabilities. In this role, you will lead and mature the processes used to track, govern, and manage hardware and software assets throughout their lifecycles. You will partner with Procurement, Finance, Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, End User Technology, Application teams, and other stakeholders to improve asset visibility, strengthen controls, support audits, optimize software licensing, and enable data-driven decisions. You will also help ensure our IT Asset Management tooling, processes, and data remain accurate, scalable, and aligned with ITIL and industry best practices. You are An experienced IT Asset Management professional who is passionate about establishing trusted asset data, strong lifecycle controls, and effective governance across enterprise hardware and software Excel at balancing operational discipline, license compliance, cost optimization, audit readiness, and partnership across technology and business teams You have Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. 5+ years of hands-on experience in IT Asset Management, including responsibility for hardware and software asset lifecycle management. Proven experience establishing or operating ITAM governance, policies, controls, inventory practices, compliance processes, and audit support in a complex enterprise environment. Experience managing software licensing and compliance activities, including entitlement tracking, normalization, reconciliation, renewals, reclamation, and optimization. Experience with a software asset management tool such as ServiceNow Software Asset Management Professional (SAMPro), Flexera, or a comparable enterprise solution. Working knowledge of hardware asset management concepts, inventory controls, asset lifecycle practices, and relationships among asset, procurement, discovery, endpoint, and CMDB data. Understanding of common software licensing models and the ability to interpret licensing, entitlement, and usage data to identify compliance risk and optimization opportunities. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to decision-making and continuous improvement. Ability to develop meaningful ITAM metrics, dashboards, compliance reporting, and executive-level insights. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical, financial, procurement, security, legal, and business stakeholders. Experience managing cross-functional initiatives and driving accountability where ownership spans multiple teams. Strong understanding of IT Service Management processes and ITIL principles; ITIL 4 Foundation certification is a plus. IT Asset Management or vendor-specific certifications such as IAITAM, ServiceNow CIS-SAM/CIS-HAM, or Flexera certifications are a plus. Familiarity with relevant governance, security, and control frameworks such as COBIT and NIST is advantageous. You will Define, implement, and continuously improve the enterprise IT Asset Management (ITAM) strategy, operating model, standards, and governance for hardware and software assets. Own and govern end-to-end hardware asset lifecycle processes, including request, procurement, receipt, inventory, assignment, movement, refresh, reuse, return, retirement, and secure disposal. Own and govern software asset lifecycle processes, including software inventory, entitlement and license tracking, normalization, reconciliation, compliance, renewals, reclamation, and retirement. Establish and enforce policies, procedures, roles, controls, and data standards that promote accurate, complete, and audit-ready asset records. Monitor hardware and software asset data quality, lifecycle compliance, inventory accuracy, license position, and exceptions using dashboards, KPIs, and recurring controls. Lead software license compliance and optimization activities, helping identify unused or underutilized licenses, contractual risk, and opportunities to reduce software spend. Partner with Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Finance, Cybersecurity, Legal, Infrastructure, End User Technology, and application owners to align asset management with purchasing, contracts, risk, financial controls, and technology standards. Support software publisher audits, internal audits, regulatory examinations, and other assurance activities by maintaining supporting records, evidence, and repeatable controls. Administer, optimize, or provide functional leadership on ServiceNow’s Software Asset Management Professional. Partner with platform and technical teams to improve integrations with discovery, endpoint management, procurement, contract, financial, and configuration management data sources. Ensure appropriate alignment and reconciliation between asset records and related configuration data while maintaining clear distinction between financial/lifecycle asset management and configuration management objectives. Develop and communicate ITAM metrics and insights to leadership, including inventory accuracy, lifecycle status, license compliance, software utilization, audit findings, cost avoidance, savings opportunities, and control effectiveness. Drive remediation of asset management exceptions and compliance gaps, escalating material risks as appropriate. Create and maintain process documentation, operational procedures, governance standards, training materials, and stakeholder communications. Promote IT Asset Management best practices across the organization and serve as a subject matter expert for hardware, software, licensing, governance, and lifecycle management. Drive continuous improvement and increasing automation of ITAM processes while favoring sustainable, platform-native capabilities over unnecessary customization. Reporting directly to the Head of Employment Law you will provide practical, business-focused legal advice on a broad range of employment matters affecting Guardian’s employees and field force. As Employment Law Counsel, you will partner closely with Human Resources, business leaders, and Law Department colleagues to manage legal risk, support sound decision-making, and advance Guardian’s business priorities. Experience with AWS data services and modern cloud data platforms, including Amazon S3, PostgreSQL, and Databricks. Demonstrated expertise with data sourcing, profiling, data mapping and data analysis. Expert SQL skills, including complex query development, performance optimization, data transformations, and scalable data-structure design. Job Title: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability
Job Description: Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability Reports To Head of Technology Operations Department Enterprise Technology Position Summary The Head of Enterprise Monitoring and Observability is responsible for defining and executing the enterprise observability strategy, operating model, and platform roadmap that enable proactive, predictive, and resilient technology operations. This leader owns the enterprise capabilities for monitoring, telemetry, event intelligence, operational analytics, and observability engineering, ensuring technology services are observable, measurable, actionable, and continuously improving. The role serves as the operational intelligence leader across Enterprise Technology, providing the platforms, standards, insights, and governance required to improve service reliability, accelerate issue detection and resolution, and support modern operational practices. This leader partners closely with infrastructure, cloud, middleware, application, security, resiliency, and service management teams to build a unified enterprise-wide observability capability. Key Responsibilities Enterprise Observability Strategy Define and execute the enterprise observability vision, strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap. Establish standards and governance for monitoring, logging, metrics, tracing, telemetry, alerting, and service observability. Lead the evolution of observability capabilities from reactive monitoring toward proactive, predictive, and automated operations. Drive enterprise adoption of modern observability practices, frameworks, and engineering standards. Observability Platform Ownership Own the strategy, architecture, lifecycle, and operation of enterprise monitoring and observability platforms. Lead platform modernization, tool rationalization, capability expansion, and service offering improvements. Manage vendor relationships, contracts, platform investments, and cost optimization efforts. Ensure scalability, availability, resilience, and ongoing enhancement of observability tooling and services. Monitoring and Telemetry Services Establish enterprise monitoring and instrumentation standards across infrastructure, cloud, middleware, applications, databases, and digital services. Improve monitoring coverage, telemetry quality, alert effectiveness, signal quality, and operational visibility. Drive adoption of distributed tracing, service dependency mapping, and end-to-end transaction monitoring. Ensure service health and operational data are consistently available across the technology landscape. Operational Intelligence and AIOps Lead implementation of operational analytics, event intelligence, anomaly detection, predictive insights, and AIOps capabilities. Develop dashboards, scorecards, and reporting that provide actionable operational intelligence to technology leadership. Enable intelligent event correlation, noise reduction, automated diagnostics, and automated operational workflows. Partner with engineering and operations teams to use observability data for continuous improvement and outage prevention. Reliability and Incident Enablement Partner with technology teams to improve detection, response, recovery, and root cause analysis capabilities. Establish observability practices that improve service reliability, operational resilience, and customer experience. Drive post-incident learning and identification of automation opportunities. Provide enterprise visibility into technology health, performance trends, capacity risks, and reliability risks. Leadership and Talent Development Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of observability engineers, platform engineers, and operational intelligence specialists. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, operational excellence, continuous learning, and cross-functional partnership. Lead organizational adoption of observability best practices through enablement, coaching, and stakeholder engagement. Establish strong partnerships across technology, cybersecurity, architecture, engineering, operations, resiliency, and service management functions. Qualifications 10+ years of experience in infrastructure operations, platform engineering, observability, reliability engineering, or related technology disciplines. 5+ years of experience leading enterprise-scale engineering or operational teams. Deep expertise in observability platforms, monitoring technologies, telemetry pipelines, logging, metrics, distributed tracing, and operational analytics. Demonstrated experience implementing enterprise monitoring strategies and improving operational reliability at scale. Strong understanding of cloud platforms, hybrid infrastructure, automation, DevOps practices, and modern operational architectures. Experience leading organizational transformation and driving adoption of new operational capabilities. Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and strategic planning skills. Success Measures Increased enterprise monitoring and observability coverage. Reduced mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR). Improved signal quality and reduced alert fatigue. Increased adoption of observability standards and platform capabilities. Improved service reliability, operational resilience, and operational efficiency. Expansion of predictive analytics, automation, and AIOps capabilities across Enterprise Technology. Job Description: Position Summary Do you want to help engineer the cloud security capabilities that protect Guardian’s applications, data, and technology as we continue to expand our use of AWS? Guardian is seeking a Senior Cloud Security Engineer to implement and continuously improve security capabilities across our cloud environment. Reporting to the Head of Security Platforms, this role will serve as a senior technical contributor across Cloud-Native Application Protection (CNAPP), Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM), AWS-native identity security controls and services, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and other cloud security controls within a complex, highly regulated environment. This role is responsible for translating security and architecture requirements into scalable engineering solutions, strengthening controls across the cloud lifecycle from code to runtime, and helping teams identify and address cloud security risk. The successful candidate will partner closely with Cloud Engineering, DevOps, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Compliance, and application teams to automate security controls, perform advanced threat and security analysis, improve cloud security posture, and enable the secure adoption of AWS services. You are A hands-on cloud security engineer who can translate complex security requirements into practical, scalable solutions. Experienced working across cloud engineering, cybersecurity, architecture, DevOps, and application teams to solve security challenges without creating unnecessary friction. Analytical and curious, with the ability to assess cloud security risks, identify gaps, and drive technical improvements from design through runtime. Comfortable operating in a complex, fast-paced environment, balancing multiple priorities while maintaining a strong focus on security, resiliency, and compliance. A strong communicator who can explain technical risks and solutions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Passionate about staying current with emerging cloud threats, security technologies, and engineering practices. Bold, relentless, curious, and collaborative, with a desire to make an impact as part of a transformational organization. You have (Required Qualifications ): 5+ years of experience in IT, cybersecurity, cloud engineering, or related disciplines. 5+ years of hands-on AWS security experience, including strong knowledge of IAM, PKI, CSPM, and CNAPP capabilities. Hands-on experience designing and implementing AWS identity controls, including IAM Identity Center, least-privilege policies, Service Control Policies (SCPs), cross-account access, and RBAC/ABAC models. Experience deploying and managing AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), and enterprise PKI capabilities. Experience implementing or operating CNAPP and CSPM platforms, such as Wiz, Prisma Cloud, and AWS Security Hub for posture management, workload protection, risk prioritization, and remediation. Strong understanding of cloud security principles, including zero trust, encryption at rest and in transit, workload and container security, identity boundaries, and network security. Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and security automation using technologies such as Terraform, CloudFormation, CI/CD pipelines, and shift-left security practices. Experience with security and compliance frameworks such as NIST, CIS, SOC 2, SOX, NYDFS, and Model Audit Rule (MAR), as well as the AWS Well-Architected Framework Security Pillar. Preferred Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Experience supporting security technology evaluations, including RFP/RFI processes, vendor assessments, and proofs of concept. Relevant certifications such as AWS Certified Security - Specialty, CISSP, or CCSP are preferred. You will (Responsibilities): Implement, and continuously improve AWS security capabilities spanning identity, cryptography and PKI, cloud security posture, and cloud-native application protection. Engineer scalable AWS access controls, including IAM policies, SCPs, cross-account access models, and least-privilege patterns. Implement and enhance cloud security controls for continuous monitoring, threat detection, vulnerability management, workload protection, and automated remediation across the application lifecycle. Integrate AWS security capabilities with enterprise CNAPP and CSPM platforms and help operationalize security controls from code through runtime. Job Description: Position Overview: The Solution Architect is responsible for owning and shaping technical solutions at the value-stream and product level, ensuring architectural alignment, scalability, and adherence to Guardian standards. This role is hands-on and execution-oriented, partnering closely with Tech Leads, Product Owners, and delivery teams to translate business needs into sound, secure, and resilient technology solutions. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. The Solution Architect focuses on solution design, delivery enablement, and technical problem solving, building solutions while collaborating with Business stakeholders, Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to align with broader enterprise patterns. Key Responsibilities: Owns product/team-level solution design and delivery architecture Works with Principal Solution Architect for patterns/guardrails; Head of Portfolio Architecture for BU priorities; Principal Enterprise Architect only when enterprise exceptions or cross-domain conflicts arise Own product- and team-level technical architecture decisions within a value stream. Design and document solution architectures, including application, integration, data, and infrastructure components. Partner with Product Owners and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Ensure solutions follow Guardian architecture standards, security requirements, and design patterns. Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to reuse enterprise capabilities where appropriate. Identify, manage, and help resolve technical dependencies and impediments impacting delivery. Provide hands-on guidance to teams on design quality, code structure, and technical approaches. Lead proof-of-concepts for new business capabilities, Influencing Technology Strategy, Solution Design, Architecture Standards. Mentor engineers on architecture principles, design decisions, and problem-solving techniques. Continuously look for opportunities to simplify designs, reduce technical debt, and improve delivery efficiency. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations You Have: Strong experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale technology solutions. Working knowledge of cloud platforms, APIs, data integration, and modern application architectures. Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience in designing hybrid architectures where applications reside both on-premise and public cloud including understanding of cloud provider services. Proven track record of architecting solutions that demand operating large scale business critical systems in Insurance domain. Good understanding of GenAI frameworks, tools and best practices Ability to balance speed, quality, risk, and long-term sustainability in technical decisions. Strong communication skills to translate technical concepts for business and delivery stakeholders. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Job Description: As the Head of AI Platform Engineering – Execution Plane, you will lead the development and implementation of our enterprise platform’s execution layer including management of agentic AI workloads, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. You will: You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and technology partners to develop and integrate automation solutions that drive business growth, improve customer experiences, and reduce operational costs. You have: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, management or a related field. Strong people leadership experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and developing senior technical talent. Deep hands-on technical background designing, building, and operating production-grade distributed systems, AI/ML platforms, data platforms, or cloud-native runtime services. Experience leading teams responsible for the execution layer of a platform, including runtime services, model inference, retrieval, orchestration, tool invocation, workflow execution, or production AI operations. Ability to own the roadmap and delivery for execution plane capabilities such as model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, runtime adapters, MCP services, knowledge bases, retrieval pipelines, inference services, and deployment patterns. Strong understanding of data access patterns, enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector/search systems, context engineering, and governed access to systems of record. Experience building reliable, scalable, low-latency execution services with clear contracts, strong observability, graceful degradation, retry patterns, rate limits, and operational resilience. Ability to partner with control plane, developer experience, data engineering, security, architecture, operations, and domain application teams to ensure execution technologies operate behind governed platform interfaces. Proven ability to drive engineering excellence through design reviews, architecture standards, testing, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, incident response, SLOs, runbooks, and production support mechanisms. Strong understanding of enterprise security and compliance requirements for runtime execution, including identity propagation, auditability, data handling, least privilege access, secrets management, and environment isolation. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to simplify complex runtime, data, and AI execution topics for senior stakeholders while aligning teams around reusable platform patterns. You will: Experience with agentic AI systems, LLM platforms, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. Experience with AWS-based AI execution services and cloud-native patterns, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, EKS, DynamoDB, S3, IAM, CloudWatch, and related DevOps tooling. Familiarity with RAG systems, enterprise search, vector databases, embedding models, rerankers, knowledge bases, context engineering, and governed retrieval from enterprise data sources. Experience designing multi-tenant runtime platforms with environment isolation, workload identities, RBAC/ABAC, cross-account access patterns, quotas, throttling, and secure service-to-service communication. Background in MLOps, LLMOps, AIOps, model lifecycle management, evaluation pipelines, model serving, inference optimization, or production AI operations. Experience with observability for AI workloads, including distributed tracing, token usage, latency, model/tool errors, cost attribution, quality metrics, safety metrics, and operational dashboards. Experience with performance, scalability, and cost optimization for high-volume runtime services, including caching, batching, streaming, load testing, capacity planning, and GPU/CPU optimization where applicable. Experience building reusable platform abstractions, SDKs, runtime adapters, reference architectures, or deployment templates that make execution technologies portable across vendors and use cases. Experience integrating enterprise tools, APIs, data services, and workflow systems through governed connectors rather than point-to-point application wiring. Comfort operating in a regulated, matrixed environment where production safety, auditability, resiliency, and vendor optionality are core design principles. Job Title: Indexed Annuity Product Investment Management Lead (Hybrid)
Job Description: Position Summary Do you want to shape how Guardian's annuity solutions deliver value to clients? Do you enjoy working across the full spectrum of investment due diligence, strategy, and management while working closely with distribution partners to explain how a strategy works and why it matters? At Guardian, we do the right thing, we believe people count, we courageously shape our future together, and we go above and beyond for the people we serve. If these values resonate with you, Guardian is seeking an Indexed Product Investment Management Lead to own the index and investment strategy agenda behind our Fixed Indexed Annuity (FIA) and Registered Index-Linked Annuity (RILA) products in close partnership with the Head of Indexed Annuities. You are An investment-minded product professional who understands what sits behind indexed crediting strategies and quality investment strategies. You are comfortable evaluating index construction and index provider proposals, discussing option budgets and hedging cost with actuarial and ALM partners, and translating all of it into a clear, credible story for advisors and clients. You are equally at home in a technical rate-setting discussion and in front of a distribution audience, and you keep a sharp eye on how index and strategy choices affect competitiveness, profitability, operations, and disclosure obligations. You have Required : A bachelor's degree (preferred), or equivalent related work experience; CFA, FRM, or actuarial credentials are a plus. 5+ years of experience in investments, derivatives, hedging, annuity pricing, or index-linked product management. Working knowledge of index construction, options and option pricing, hedge budgets, and how crediting mechanics such as caps, participation rates, spreads, buffers, floors, and triggers are funded. Strong executive and technical communication skills, with the ability to make complex investment concepts clear and accurate for internal partners, advisors, and clients. Comfort and credibility in market-facing settings, including wholesaler enablement, firm due diligence, and advisor education. Strong analytical capability, financial acumen, and sound business judgment, with rigorous attention to accuracy in data, performance figures, and competitive comparisons. Excellent influencing, organizational, and facilitation skills; able to gain consensus and cultivate strategic internal and external relationships. Ability to manage several dissimilar projects concurrently and prioritize appropriately in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Preferred : Direct FIA and/or RILA experience. Familiarity with index provider relationships, licensing agreements, and the disclosure and filing obligations that accompany index use in annuity products. Experience leveraging AI tools to enhance and accelerate results. You will Drive the index and crediting strategy agenda across Guardian's FIA and RILA portfolio, including the current index menu, term lengths, and crediting methods, and recommend additions, replacements, and retirements aligned to product strategy. Lead research and development on new indices and investment strategies, including engagement with index providers, investment banks, and asset management partners, and assessment of internal and operational implications. Evaluate proposed indices on construction, historical and expected behavior, volatility control mechanics, option cost and hedgeability, illustration eligibility, and fit with target advisor and client use cases. Partner with Annuity Pricing, Hedging, and ALM on option budgets, hedge feasibility, and the economics of custom versus benchmark indices. Support the monthly new business and renewal rate-setting process with competitive and investment perspective on cap, participation, spread, and trigger levels, and on the in-force renewal rate path. Monitor and explain index and strategy performance across new business and the in-force block, and partner closely with marketing on clear materials that help advisors, wholesalers, and clients understand results and opportunities. Serve as the market-facing subject matter expert on our investment and crediting strategies, supporting wholesaler training, firm and home-office conversations, due diligence requests, and advisor education. Negotiate and manage index licensing relationships in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and Sourcing, including fee structures, use rights, disclosure obligations, and notice and termination provisions. Coordinate the operational and regulatory requirements that follow index decisions, including index disclosures in contracts, prospectuses, illustrations, marketing materials, and state filings, and the procedures that apply if an index is closed or terminated. Account for jurisdictional and regulatory constraints in strategy design, including state specific product limitations and state illustration rules that restrict how indices with limited history may be illustrated. Conduct due diligence on variable annuity fund management and provide investment thought leadership to other annuity product teams as needed. Bring competitive intelligence on carrier index menus, crediting innovation, and rate positioning into product design, rate-setting, and positioning decisions. Reporting Relationships As our Indexed Product Investment Management Lead, you will report to our Head of Indexed Annuities, who reports to our Head of Annuities. Location The primary location for this position is Hudson Yards, New York, but we are also open to candidates who can commute into our Holmdel, NJ, Bethlehem, PA, Pittsfield, MA, Stamford, CT, or Boston, MA offices at least 3-days per week. Travel 10% travel may be required for this position. Strong customer service, consultative, negotiation, persuasion, and influencing skills. Analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the ability to interpret experience reports, utilization trends, pricing analysis, and plan design options. Working knowledge of group insurance products, contracts, services, financing methodologies, and underwriting principles. Ability to build and maintain collaborative relationships across clients, brokers, sales teams, underwriting, service, and claims organizations. Strong planning, organizational, and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing business needs. Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience. Insurance industry experience within a sales, account management, customer-facing, or client management environment. Knowledge of ancillary group insurance products, including dental, vision, life, accident, disability, statutory benefits, supplemental health, voluntary benefits, and leave management. Knowledge of fully insured and alternate funding arrangements and related underwriting practices. Experience identifying cross-sell opportunities and supporting retention, renewal, and add-issue strategies. Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Job Description: Position Summary Do you enjoy turning complex data into meaningful business insights and translating those insights into compensation strategies that drive sales performance? Guardian's Group Distribution Compensation team is seeking a Senior Sales Compensation Analyst to lead complex analysis, administration, design, and continuous improvement of incentive compensation programs for our Group Sales Distribution organization. In this role, you will serve as a strategic and consultative partner to senior business leaders, independently lead high-impact compensation initiatives, collaborate across functions, and leverage advanced analytics, automation, and emerging technologies to strengthen decision-making. You will help ensure compensation programs are accurate, scalable, well-governed, and aligned with evolving business priorities and sales strategies. You Are A highly analytical and solutions-oriented professional who brings sound judgment, business acumen, and a continuous improvement mindset to complex work. You are comfortable operating with a high degree of independence, translating ambiguous business needs into practical solutions, and influencing stakeholders through clear, data-driven recommendations. You balance strategic thinking with disciplined execution, manage multiple priorities, and maintain a high level of accuracy, confidentiality, and customer focus. You also contribute to the development of team capabilities by sharing expertise, establishing effective practices, and providing guidance to others. You Have Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. 6+ years of progressive professional experience in sales compensation, compensation, finance, sales operations, business analytics, payroll, or a related field. Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data, identify trends and anomalies, evaluate business impact, and develop actionable recommendations. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications, including the ability to build and validate complex models and reporting tools. Demonstrated experience working with large and complex datasets, reconciling information across multiple sources, and producing accurate executive-level reporting. Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex compensation concepts, influence decisions, and tailor communications for senior leadership and varied stakeholder audiences. Preferred Qualifications Deep experience administering complex sales incentive compensation programs, including plan governance, payment validation, and issue resolution. Strong knowledge of compensation design, financial modeling, plan mechanics, controls, and end-to-end plan administration. Experience with Microsoft Access, Visual Basic, SQL, data visualization tools, or comparable technologies used to automate and enhance analysis and reporting. Experience supporting large or complex sales organizations, distribution teams, or multiple compensation plans and channels. Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional projects involving compensation, payroll, finance, sales performance, systems, or process transformation. Experience applying AI-enabled tools, automation, advanced analytics, or data visualization to improve reporting, decision-making, controls, and operational efficiency. You Will Lead the end-to-end administration of complex sales incentive compensation programs, including payment calculations, validation, exception management, payroll coordination, and timely delivery of accurate reporting. Own advanced analysis and modeling across multiple data sources to assess plan performance, identify risks and opportunities, resolve discrepancies, and provide actionable insights that support business decisions. Partner with senior leadership to evaluate, model, design, and implement annual incentive compensation plans and strategic enhancements aligned with business objectives, sales strategy, and financial parameters. Develop and deliver executive-ready presentations, plan documents, analytics, and performance reporting that clearly communicate compensation program design, results, risks, and recommended actions. Serve as a subject matter expert and lead compensation workstreams supporting new products, distribution channels, organizational changes, system enhancements, and other strategic business initiatives. Build trusted relationships with sales leaders and key business partners across Finance, Payroll, HR, Legal, Technology, and Sales Operations to anticipate needs, provide guidance, and influence decisions through data-driven recommendations. Establish and maintain strong governance, documentation, and quality controls; proactively assess risks and support audit, compliance, and remediation activities. Lead root-cause analysis and resolution of complex compensation issues, balancing accuracy, plan intent, business impact, and stakeholder needs. Provide coaching, technical guidance, and peer review to analysts and cross-functional partners; share best practices and help strengthen team capabilities. Lead continuous improvement efforts by identifying and implementing opportunities to strengthen automation, AI-enabled capabilities, advanced analytics, reporting, scalability, controls, and the stakeholder experience. Job Description: Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a resolute motivated individual to join our team as a Senior Lead Financial Analyst. Recognized as the Client Solutions & Wealth Management (CSWM) subject-matter expert in financial and business analytics, the Financial Analyst, Wealth Management sets the analytical agenda that turns Park Avenue Wealth Management (PAWM) and Guardian Wealth Partners (GWP) into decisions. Operating with mastery-level expertise and little day-to-day oversight, this role owns the margin, profitability, and performance insight that shapes how the business allocates capital, prices and serves clients, and invests in growth. This role provides recommendations and supports business cases directly to inform decisions made by CSWM and enterprise leaders, and it contributes to the functional strategy for how Finance partners with the business. You will: • Drive financial planning & analysis for the PAWM business — lead planning, forecasting, and the management-reporting P&L; surface the key drivers and trends; and own the critical view of PAWM channel economics — margin at channel, client, and producer level — translating it into insight that drives capital allocation, pricing, and growth decisions. • Develop the business cases and ROI frameworks that govern enablement and investment decisions across distribution, channel, and expense (including Clearing & Execution) economics. • Lead complex, high-visibility analytical initiatives with notable risk and cross-functional dependencies — defining the execution strategy, not just the analysis — such as net-flow and margin insight, distribution economics, and cost-to-serve. • Build and own the financial models behind budgeting, forecasting, driver-based planning, and long-range planning for PAWM/GWP, setting the standard others build to. • Convey and communicate complex findings to senior leaders — translating analysis into clear recommendations that support decision-making across Finance and the business, including through effective presentations. • Act as advisor, mentor, and technical authority to colleagues at all levels, raising the analytical capability of the broader team. • Contribute to the functional finance strategy for PAWM/GWP — shaping how the team industrializes data, embeds AI/automation, and shifts from reporting toward strategic partnership. You are: • Resourceful and relentlessly curious, you transform a conceptual analytical framework into tangible insight by understanding the relationships between data and the business rules and processes that produce it. • Comfortable operating with minimal oversight in a complex environment, you independently locate, reconcile, and validate data, flagging and resolving issues before they become problems. • A confident communicator who develops a deep understanding of complex topics and translates results for stakeholders in clear, non-technical terms, iterating with leadership and subject-matter experts to rationalize and refine the value of your analysis — and to persuade when the answer is not the expected one. • A recognized expert others seek out — you anticipate where the business is heading and bring the analysis forward before the question is asked. You have: Required: • 7+ years' experience developing and presenting financial and business analytics, including to senior leadership. • 7+ years' experience analyzing financial statements and interpreting results, with mastery of the drivers behind them. • Advanced experience with Excel and other data/analytics tools, comfort building repeatable processes over large, complex, multi-source datasets, and fluency in applying automation and AI to industrialize analysis. Preferred: • Experience with Wealth Management economics in a financial services or insurance arena. • A track record of leading complex, cross-functional analytical initiatives with notable risk, and of influencing decisions beyond your own team. • Experience working across multiple business areas and/or lines of business (e.g., sales, finance, life, disability, wealth/brokerage, distribution), and demonstrated knowledge of the concepts, processes, and datasets inherent to those environments. • Experience partnering with multiple stakeholders in a fast driven environment. Job Description: The Principal Enterprise Architect is a senior architecture leader responsible for shaping, guiding, and advancing enterprise architecture across the organization. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Enablement , this role translates enterprise strategy into practical architecture direction, standards, target-state designs, and transition roadmaps across business capabilities, applications, platforms, data, integration, cloud, security, and emerging technology domains. While architecture is foundation al, the Principal Enterprise Architect will be responsible for design ing enterprise solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders . Where applicable the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale for the enterprise. This position plays a critical role in connecting enterprise strategy to federated execution. The Principal Enterprise Architect partners with architecture, engineering, platform, security, data, and business technology leaders to ensure material technology decisions align with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, modernization priorities, and governance requirements. The role requires strong strategic thinking, architecture breadth, executive communication, and the ability to influence across a large, complex, and federated enterprise environment. The Principal Enterprise Architect provides architecture leadership and recommendations on material technology decisions and has delegated authority within the enterprise architecture operating model as assigned by the Head of Enterprise Architecture. The role is expected to escalate decisions with enterprise-wide impact, non-standard exceptions, or significant risk implications. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Architecture Leadership Support the Head of Enterprise Architecture in developing and evolving enterprise architecture strategy , principles, standards, and target-state roadmaps. Define and maintain architecture perspectives across business, application, data, integration, cloud, platform, security, and AI-related capabilities as applicable. Own enterprise standards, target state, governance, exceptions, material technology decision frameworks Translate enterprise strategy and target-state direction into practical guidance for domain architecture and engineering teams. Promote alignment across business units, shared services, and technology domains. Strategic Architecture and Transformation Provide architecture leadership for major strategic initiatives, modernization programs, and enterprise-impacting technology decisions. Assess architecture options and recommend solutions that balance business value, cost, risk, resilience, time to market, and long-term maintainability. Support enterprise transformation through simplification, rationalization, modernization, and platform reuse. Identify opportunities to reduce duplication, retire legacy complexity, and improve interoperability across the enterprise. Governance and Decision Support Participate in and support enterprise architecture governance, standards councils, review boards, and strategic decision forums. Evaluate material technology decisions using approved enterprise frameworks, including buy, build, reuse, partner, and retire options. Review architecture proposals for compliance with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, and risk requirements. Support management of architecture exceptions, including rationale, risk analysis, remediation paths, and time-bound approvals. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with federated domain architects, platform leaders, engineering teams, data and AI teams, security, infrastructure, and business technology leaders to drive alignment. Facilitate resolution of cross-domain design issues, architecture conflicts, and overlapping capability decisions. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across technology and business-aligned delivery organizations. Ensure architecture direction is understood and applied consistently across federated teams. Works with Business Unit heads and principal solution architects to translate enterprise direction into federated execution. Risk, Security, and Resilience Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, recoverability, and regulatory considerations into architecture guidance and recommendations. Partner with risk, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure technology decisions align with enterprise control requirements. Assess the operational and architectural implications of technology choices in regulated and high-availability environments. Talent and Capability Development Mentor and coach architects and senior technology professionals. Contribute to architecture capability development, communities of practice, and architecture operating model maturity. Support common role expectations, competency models, and quality standards across the architecture function. Promote enterprise-first thinking, sound decision-making, and strong architecture discipline. You Have: Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science , Information Systems, Engineering, or related field. 1 2 + years of progressive experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, domain architecture, or senior technology strategy roles. Deep cross-domain expertise spanning applications, integration, data, AI, cloud, security, and platform strategy. Experience supporting or leading architecture for large-scale transformation initiatives in complex enterprise environments. Experience with architecture governance, standards development, target-state planning, and strategic technology decision-making. Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority. Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Preferred Education and Experience Experience in insurance, financial services, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry. Experience in a federated technology organization with centralized architecture direction and distributed execution. Experience with cloud modernization, API strategies, platform engineering, data ecosystems, and enterprise integration. Familiarity with AI-enabled enterprise capabilities, automation, and emerging technology trends. Advanced degree and/or relevant certifications such as TOGAF, SAFe , AWS, Azure, GCP, or equivalent. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture principles, methods, and governance practices. Broad understanding of enterprise technology domains and cross-domain dependencies. Ability to develop target-state architecture and pragmatic transition approaches. Strong business acumen and ability to connect architecture decisions to business outcomes. Ability to assess tradeoffs among speed, cost, quality, risk, and strategic fit. Strong facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to communicate effectively with executive, business, and technical audiences. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and lead through influence. Job Description: Position Summary Are you passionate about helping employees make informed benefits decisions while driving exceptional client outcomes? Do you thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where you can influence strategy, solve complex challenges, and build strong partnerships? Guardian is seeking an Enrollment Practice Leader to lead the end-to-end enrollment experience for our sales partners, brokers, employers, and members. In this role, you will serve as a trusted enrollment expert responsible for managing complex, high-impact cases, driving enrollment success, and delivering exceptional service experiences. You will partner across Sales, Client Management, and Enrollment teams to execute strategic enrollment solutions while identifying opportunities to improve processes, increase engagement, and support the continued growth of Guardian's enrollment capabilities. You Are A strategic and client-focused enrollment professional who thrives at the intersection of operational execution, relationship management, and enrollment consulting. You are energized by managing complex enrollment initiatives and collaborating with internal partners, brokers, and employers to deliver outstanding enrollment experiences. You have the ability to assess unique client needs, influence decisions, and develop creative solutions that drive participation and successful outcomes. You excel in environments where balancing multiple priorities, managing stakeholder expectations, and solving complex challenges are critical to success. You are a trusted advisor who leverages deep enrollment expertise, industry knowledge, and strong communication skills to guide clients and internal teams through the enrollment process. Success in this role requires a relentless focus on client outcomes, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and helping employees make informed benefits decisions that best meet their needs and those of their families. You Have Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience. 5+ years of experience in group benefits enrollment, benefits administration, client management, or a related field. Proven success managing high-volume and high-impact enrollment activities with measurable results. Experience supporting enrollment strategies, including one-on-one enrollments, decision support tools, digital enrollment campaigns, and employee education programs. Strong understanding of group benefits products and enrollment best practices. Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and lead initiatives across multiple teams and business partners. Experience mentoring team members and sharing operational best practices. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify process improvements and implement effective solutions. Exceptional presentation, communication, and relationship-management skills. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting brokers, employer groups, and distribution partners within the employee benefits industry. Knowledge of enrollment technologies, decision support engines, and enrollment platforms. Experience leveraging enrollment data and performance metrics to improve engagement and outcomes. Experience working in a consultative, client-facing role supporting large or complex accounts. Demonstrated ability to drive operational innovation and process optimization initiatives. You Will Lead and manage the end-to-end group benefits enrollment process, ensuring accurate execution, operational efficiency, and exceptional client outcomes. Serve as the primary Guardian Enrollment contact for distribution partners, brokers, employers, and internal stakeholders throughout the enrollment lifecycle. Gather enrollment requirements, coordinate case-level activities, and execute enrollment deliverables to support successful enrollment events. Job Title: Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation
Job Description: The Head of Product Strategy & Platform Innovation is a senior leadership role responsible for the strategic evolution, differentiation, and commercial success of our open‑architecture wealth management product platform. This individual wakes up every day thinking about what’s next —how product, partners, packaging, and go‑to‑market strategy come together to create a compelling, modern, and advisor‑centric platform across fee‑based advisory, annuities, and alternatives. We do not manufacture products. Our competitive advantage comes from curation, partnership, design, positioning, and delivery . This role exists to ensure our platform is not merely comprehensive—but distinctive, relevant, and growth‑oriented . The role works horizontally across the organization —marketing, sales, business development, training, product management—and externally with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and portfolio managers . Success requires influence without direct ownership, entrepreneurial energy, and a strong commercial mindset. Key Responsibilities Product Strategy & Innovation Own the forward‑looking product strategy across advisory, annuities, and alternatives within an open‑architecture ecosystem. Identify gaps, white spaces, and emerging opportunities driven by advisor needs, client behavior, regulation, and competitive dynamics. Design differentiated product constructs, solutions, and portfolios by creatively leveraging third‑party partners rather than manufacturing products. Translate industry trends (e.g., retirement income, tax efficiency, private markets, managed solutions, model portfolios) into actionable platform initiatives. Platform Differentiation & Go‑to‑Market Develop clear go‑to‑market strategies for platform capabilities, including positioning, messaging, and advisor value propositions. Partner closely with Marketing to ensure product stories are simple, compelling, and commercially effective . Work with Sales and Business Development to align product strategy with advisor adoption, growth objectives, and field readiness . Drive clarity around why advisors should use specific solutions—not just what is available. Partner Strategy & Ecosystem Management Serve as a senior point of engagement with asset managers, insurance carriers, TAMPs, and product sponsors . Evaluate, onboard, and rationalize partners with a focus on quality, differentiation, economics, and strategic fit . Co‑create solutions with partners where appropriate, including custom portfolios, white‑labeled offerings, or exclusive access strategies . Maintain a strong commercial lens on platform economics, scalability, and advisor impact. Cross‑Functional Leadership & Influence Act as a strategic connector across Product Management, Sales, Marketing, Training, and Business Development. Provide strategic direction while leveraging existing execution teams for implementation. Influence priorities and outcomes without direct people ownership , using clarity, credibility, and collaboration. Partner with Training and Sales Enablement to ensure advisors understand not just products—but how to use them in holistic planning conversations . What Success Looks Like Advisors view the platform as thoughtful, differentiated, and easy to position with clients . Product initiatives are clearly linked to advisor adoption, client outcomes, and revenue growth . Partners see the firm as a strategic collaborator , not just a distributor. The platform evolves proactively— not reactively —to market and advisor needs. Qualifications & Experience 10+ years of experience in wealth management, asset management, insurance, or fintech, with exposure to RIA and broker‑dealer environments . Deep knowledge of fee‑based advisory, annuities, alternatives, and managed solutions . Demonstrated ability to build or evolve open‑architecture platforms without manufacturing products. Strong commercial and go‑to‑market orientation —understands how strategy translates into advisor behavior. Proven success working cross‑functionally and influencing outcomes without direct authority. Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to balance vision with practical execution . Comfortable operating with ambiguity and turning ideas into scalable initiatives. Why This Role Matters This role ensures our product platform moves from “robust but pedestrian” to strategically curated, commercially sharp, and advisor‑obsessed —without disrupting what already works operationally. It complements strong execution with vision, innovation, and market leadership .
