Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. You Have (Required Qualifications) : Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level. Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority. Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs. Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities. Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Additional Data-Focused Qualifications Required : Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms, data products, or analytics capabilities. Strong understanding of modern data architecture principles, including data mesh, data products, metadata, governance, and domain-driven design. Experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Kafka, or similar technologies. Experience rolling out AI capabilities or AI-enabled solutions within a data ecosystem. Experience within insurance industry, including enrollment, eligibility, policy administration, billing, claims, customer data, and employer administration. Expertise in cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. Strong programming and data engineering skills in Python, PySpark, and SQL. Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills. Experience leading data product initiatives, including proof-of-concept development and feasibility assessment. Familiarity with product management methodologies and Agile frameworks. Success Measures: Increased adoption and reuse of enterprise data products. Improved business outcomes through product-driven data capabilities. Faster delivery of business initiatives through reusable platforms and engineering accelerators. Increased adoption of AI-powered solutions across organization. Higher data quality, trust, discoverability, and governance. Strong cross-functional alignment between business, product, engineering, architecture, and data organizations. This role is accountable for optimizing learning and development, quality assurance programs, underwriting tools, data and operational metrics and capacity while ensuring leaders and teams are fully prepared to adopt new ways of working. This leader will embed best practices, enable accurate and consistent decision-making, and cultivate a culture of continuous improvement while proactively preparing the organization for operational, technological, and capability change. A central responsibility of this role is to ensure underwriting excellence is achieved and sustained through strong execution, readiness, and adoption. Develop and execute operational excellence strategies aligned to underwriting goals, enterprise priorities, and customer outcomes. Establish performance metrics, benchmarks, and KPIs to measure operational success, decision quality, and underwriting productivity. Utilize data analytics and underwriting tools to generate insights, inform decisions, and proactively optimize execution. Manage quality assurance programs that surface risk, consistency, and training needs—ensuring issues are addressed systematically and sustainably. Partner closely with cross-functional teams to help implement technology solutions and process changes that enhance underwriting workflows and decision-making. Organizational Readiness & Change Leadership Act as a primary owner of organizational readiness for underwriting process, technology, and capability changes. Assess change impact and readiness across underwriting teams, translating operational initiatives into clear people, role, skill, and behavior implications. Lead and embed change enablement practices that ensure smooth adoption of new processes, tools, and operating models. Partner with underwriting leaders to strengthen change leadership capability, ensuring leaders actively sponsor, reinforce, and role-model new ways of working. Identify adoption risks and cultural barriers early, implementing mitigation strategies that support sustained behavioral change. Ensure operational improvements are reinforced through updated operating rhythms, performance expectations, governance, and training—not just documented outcomes. Capability & Culture Building Design and implement best-in-class training programs that elevate underwriting capability, consistency, and decision quality. Provide ongoing support, tools, and resources that enable colleagues to work more efficiently and confidently. Engage stakeholders at all levels to foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and urgent execution. Instill a strong linkage between operational excellence, consumer-centricity, and underwriting excellence. Job Description: Position Summary The Workday Technical Lead – Payroll, Time & Absence is responsible for the end-to-end technical ownership, design, and governance of Workday Payroll, Time Tracking, and Absence modules. This role serves as the system authority for the domain, ensuring scalable design, data integrity, and alignment with business and compliance requirements. This position operates within IT and partners closely with Payroll, HR, and external vendors to deliver reliable, efficient, and compliant solutions. While not responsible for payroll processing, this role is accountable for the systems and configurations that enable accurate payroll outcomes. Key Responsibilities Domain Ownership & Technical Leadership Own the architectural and configuration guardrails for Payroll, Time, and Absence, coordinating execution while retaining accountability for outcomes. Establish and maintain standards for configuration, data integrity, and system governance. Make and guide key decisions on system design, scalability, and long-term architecture. Serve as the primary escalation point for complex system and payroll-impacting issues. System Design & Configuration Lead configuration of payroll elements, time tracking rules, and absence plans with a focus on scalability and maintainability. Ensure configurations support business requirements while minimizing downstream risk. Evaluate and redesign existing configurations to improve performance, accuracy, and usability. Payroll Systems Enablement (U.S.) Ensure Workday Payroll configurations support accurate and compliant payroll processing. Partner with Payroll leadership to identify risks, gaps, and optimization opportunities. Own enterprise‑level resolution of payroll‑impacting issues, including root cause identification, risk mitigation, and long‑term remediation. Global Payroll Integration (India – External Vendor) Own design and reliability of outbound payroll data integrations. Ensure data accuracy, consistency, and auditability across systems. Coordinate with external vendors to resolve systemic issues and improve processes. Architecture, Integrations & Data Own architectural decisions and trade‑offs for payroll, time, and absence integrations, balancing compliance, scalability, and operational risk (e.g., EIB, APIs, vendor feeds) Ensure alignment between Workday and downstream/upstream systems Define and maintain data standards, controls, and validation processes Workday Release & Change Governance Lead impact assessment and strategy for Workday biannual releases Establish testing standards and ensure high-quality deployment of changes Govern system changes to ensure stability and avoid unintended impacts Continuous Improvement & Strategy Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual work, and improve system efficiency Translate business needs into scalable, forward-looking system solutions Shape and influence the broader HR technology roadmap, representing Payroll, Time, and Absence priorities and trade‑offs. Stakeholder Leadership Act as the primary technical advisor and decision partner to Payroll, HR, and IT stakeholders Provide clear recommendations and guidance on system capabilities and limitations Influence decision-making through expertise and data-driven insights Required Qualifications 5+ years of Workday experience with deep expertise in: Workday Payroll (U.S.) Time Tracking Absence Proven experience owning system design and configuration decisions Strong understanding of payroll processes, compliance, and downstream impacts Experience supporting integrations and data flows across systems Demonstrated ability to lead complex problem-solving and root cause analysis Preferred Qualifications Workday certifications in Payroll, Time Tracking, or Absence Experience with global payroll integrations and vendor coordination Experience with Workday integrations (EIB, Studio, APIs) Background in IT or HR technology environments Success Factors Operates as the accountable owner of the domain, not just a contributor Makes sound technical decisions with long-term impact in mind Balances stability with continuous improvement Anticipates risks and proactively addresses them Communicates complex technical concepts clearly to stakeholders Location : Three days a week at a Guardian office in New York, NY, Holmdel, NJ, Stamford, CT or Bethlehem, PA.
